plan_title: CapturePoint LLC Seminole East Field Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The East Seminole San Andres Unit and Lindoss Unit boundaries; the projected CO2 storage area (about 1,000 acres) sits inside the 2,045-acre field outline (p16).
mma_definition: The two unit boundaries plus a half-mile buffer, though the same paragraph also says the MMA is the same as the AMA (p16).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Wellbores and surface equipment are treated as the only meaningful pathways; faults, seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, third-party drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated low or negligible (p18-23).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is ongoing operational data (injection targets and excursion flags, production forecasts, visual inspections, H2S alarms) used to spot deviations that could indicate leakage (p29-30).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report, filed around March 31 with other GHG reports, with the mass balance and estimated leakage; well changes noted in the annual report; records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish measurement data (p4, p23, p29-30, p34, p36).

rows.detail: Custody transfer meter on CO2 received from the Kinder Morgan pipeline and an operations meter at the recycle compression facility outlet; received CO2 composition sampled at least quarterly.
rows.location: Custody transfer point; recycle compression facility outlet
rows.evidence_quote: This meter measures flow rate continually.

rows.detail: Injection pressure and rate checked against weekly pattern injection plans; SCADA monitors wellhead pressure and WAG skids are continuously monitored; excursions flagged and screened for leakage.
rows.trigger_or_response: Pressure or rate outside pattern set points: field personnel investigate; unresolved issues get detailed investigation; wellhead leak means shut-in and workover.
rows.evidence_quote: Pressure in injection wells is monitored daily.

rows.detail: Annular pressure in wellheads monitored to detect tubing and casing leaks.
rows.trigger_or_response: Anomaly: inspect; simple repair on the spot, otherwise shut in, work order, workover crew within days.
rows.evidence_quote: monitoring of the annular pressure in wellheads

rows.detail: MITs on injectors listed in the response table for tubing and casing leaks; no interval given.
rows.trigger_or_response: Tubing or casing leak: well shut in and workover crew responds within days.

rows.detail: Each producer tested about monthly at satellite test stations (12-24 hours); produced gas metered at the recycle facility inlet and sampled annually for CO2; performance compared with forecast.
rows.location: Each production well; satellite test stations; recycle compression facility inlet
rows.trigger_or_response: Significant deviation from forecast: well management personnel investigate; leakage quantified by material balance if found.
rows.evidence_quote: each well being tested approximately once every month

rows.detail: Reservoir pressure collected for operations management and routinely updated; the response table relies on pressure at WAG headers and high pressure in new wells. No observation wells or gauges named.
rows.location: WAG headers; newly drilled wells (no observation wells named)
rows.trigger_or_response: High pressure: re-enter and reseal abandoned wells, manage fluids along lease lines, keep below parting pressure, or shut in injectors near a seismic event.
rows.evidence_quote: The reservoir pressure in the SEF is collected for use in operations management.

rows.detail: Routine field visits to wells and surface facilities looking for white CO2 clouds, ice and fluid leaks; also used to spot unapproved drilling.
rows.location: Field-wide wells, surface facilities and pipelines
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak found: repair on the spot or shut in, work order, quantify for Subpart W or RR reporting.
rows.evidence_quote: Field inspections are conducted on a routine basis by field personnel.

rows.detail: All field personnel wear H2S monitors (alarm at 10 ppm); H2S, over 18,000 ppm in recycled gas, is used as a proxy for CO2 leaks.
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, investigate source, quantify CO2 leak for the annual report.
rows.evidence_quote: H2S monitors are worn by all field personnel.

rows.detail: Permanent ground-level H2S monitors throughout the field alarm at a set limit; number and locations not given.
rows.location: Field-wide at ground level (locations not specified)
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, investigate source, quantify CO2 leak.
rows.evidence_quote: there are various permanent H2S monitors throughout the field at ground level to detect H2S and alarm if a limit is reached.

rows.detail: Injection radioactive tracer survey if unexplained injection pressure changes suggest diffuse leakage through the seal.
rows.trigger_or_response: Unexplained injection pressure change: tracer survey; if verified, shut in and workover within days.
rows.evidence_quote: Conduct an injection radioactive tracer survey.

rows.detail: Operator watches the public USGS earthquake map site for signals of new leakage pathways, after a one-time review of the USGS catalog (M0.5+ since 1966); no site seismometers.
rows.trigger_or_response: Seismic event: shut in injectors near the event.
rows.evidence_quote: CapturePoint monitors the USGS earthquake monitoring Geological Information System (GIS)

rows.detail: Past seismic and geologic evidence cited as showing no faults through the reservoir; no repeat seismic.
rows.evidence_quote: After reviewing geologic, seismic, operating, and other evidence, it has been concluded that there are no known faults or fractures

rows.detail: Subpart W emission factors and engineering estimates used to quantify surface equipment leaks and vents, reconciled with event-driven leak estimates to avoid double counting.
rows.evidence_quote: CapturePoint uses 40 CFR Part 98 Subpart W to estimate surface leaks from equipment at the SEF.

rows.detail: Step-rate tests measure formation parting pressure so injection pressure can be kept below it; plan says these measurements are routinely updated.
rows.evidence_quote: Injection pressure is also maintained below the FPP, which is measured using step-rate tests.

notes: Near-identical template to CapturePoint's Wellman plan; the main differences are permanent ground-level H2S monitors and an ongoing (unscheduled) watch of the USGS earthquake site, both coded committed. The plan says injection pressure is 'monitored daily' (p19) and elsewhere 'continuously monitored' (p23); coded daily. MMA text is self-contradictory (unit boundary plus half-mile buffer, yet 'same as the AMA', p16). Reservoir pressure is said to be collected but no instruments or wells are named. Continuous water-curtain injection at the unit boundary (p9, p22) is a containment practice, not monitoring, so it is not coded. Figures and the process flow diagrams are images.
